done: ARMv5TE/ARMv4T instruction cards, conformant in every engine
direct boot of both CPUs, measured
ARM9 code lifted, identical to the interpreter
VRAM banks and both 2D engines (BG modes 0-6, OBJs, windows, blending, master brightness, screen swap)

the save chip (serial flash), SPI devices (power management, a firmware made from card data, touch screen), the RTC, the sound channels' busy bits, the geometry FIFO as an idle engine, the ARM7's BIOS sound tables
headless runs that save both screens: cardmodel machine nds ROM --png / --shots / --input

the 3D engine as hardware cards: geometry (FIFO, matrices, lighting, clipping, two polygon RAMs) and rendering (W/Z depth, Gouraud, perspective-correct textures in all seven formats, translucency); Diamond's title Dialga and its intro's flight over Sinnoh's towns
sound mixing as a hardware card: PCM8, PCM16, IMA-ADPCM, PSG and noise channels with volume, panning and the master volume; Diamond's music comes out (cardmodel machine nds ROM --wav)

direct boot as a card (machine/nds boot.card, load_image): binaries, header, chip ID, a firmware flash and user settings with their CRCs, the save chip by game code, all from the image and card data; the host and the player share it

the DS player for Cardmodel Arcade (system/nds, player.card): both screens in one picture, buttons and the touch screen, sound at the shell's rate, the save chip kept per cartridge, the clock from the shell; Pokemon Diamond at 250-320 frames per second natively

the Wi-Fi hardware as a card (nds_wifi): the register file the wireless driver tests, the baseband and RF chips, power-up and its interrupt, the microsecond counter and beacon interrupts, TX slots; Diamond's main menu starts its wireless driver, scans three channels and continues a save

the DS player's check cartridge for arcade check: a DS image (nds.check_image) whose ARM9 words come off the ARM instruction cards (asm.arm_word), drawing on both screens and writing a byte to the save chip
Pokemon Diamond: copyright and ESRB screens, intro, title screen, a new game's first dialogue
tests/test_nds.py: a synthetic image drawn by ARM9 code, every device, the player, Diamond's first screens when present
goal: Nintendo DS games running on the ARM instruction cards, lifted like the Game Boy.
left: Thumb and the ARM7 in the lifter (speed)
display capture, the main-memory display FIFO, EEPROM and FRAM save chips
edge marking, fog, anti-aliasing and shadow polygons in the 3D engine
the RTC in local time: the shell's offset from UTC (player_clock_offset)
name: ds_prototype
next_steps: MATH_CORE (approved 2026-10-22): the DS is its hardware cards, card-language semantics the semantic core can reason about and symbolically execute (2D and 3D engines, VRAM banks, SPI, RTC, IPC, sound), never host-language emulation code; emulation, screenshots, test ROMs and differential runs are witnesses, never the method

the arcade side for the DS player (the OAM session): its d80128a (the shell keeps player_clock_offset at the local UTC offset; the library lists DS cartridges as playable) on its way to main; the arcade branch's tables-optional system.py and pointer input are on main
symbolic terms for the ARM/Thumb instruction cards (MATH_CORE F5, after main's LR35902 terms), and the ARM lifter keeping its terms as cards (phase 2)
the DS hardware cards traced to the four sources (CM44): definitions for their behaviour, the methods that run and witness them
merge claude/blissful-easley-814fa6 into main (the arcade branch it needs is on main)
standing: Pokemon Diamond plays in the DS player (system/nds): a new game through the touch-screen tutorial and naming into its 3D world (walking, the menu, an in-game save kept in the player's save file), and a later boot continues that save (its main menu's wireless scan runs on the Wi-Fi card); headless 190-375 frames per second. The player needs the arcade branch's system.py and shell (a card without tables, pointer input) and is not yet installed in the arcade.
statement: Both DS CPUs direct-booted on the ARM instruction cards with VRAM, both 2D engines, the 3D engine, the sound mixer, the save chip, SPI devices, the clock and the Wi-Fi hardware as cards, and booted by a card: Pokemon Diamond plays in the DS player (system/nds) for Cardmodel Arcade, new game and continue.
